newsitem.title: UK: UK's PPL Therap achieves peptide in rabbits.
newsitem.headline: UK's PPL Therap achieves peptide in rabbits.

text.p: Britain's PPL Therapeutics, which recently helped to create Dolly the sheep, the worlds' first adult clone, said on Monday it could now produce amidated peptide in the milk of transgenic rabbits.
The peptide, expressed as a fusion protein, was detected at a concentration of one gram per litre, PPL said.

"This is the first time this class of peptide has been produced in the milk of transgenic animals offering the potential for a greater number of pharmaceutical products to be manufactured using transgenic technology," PPL said.
The research was conducted by PPL Therapeutics Inc, the U.S. division of the UK company.
"...The results confirm the ability of the mammary gland to correctly modify introduced products," the firm said.
Alan Colman, PPL's research director, described it as a "welcome surprise".
PPL has filed for patents on this approach to peptide production.
The company's share price was marked 45 pence higher at 472 1/2 after the announcement, despite it suffering a pretax loss of 6.2 million stg in 1996.
